 Aaron Nesmith (hamstring) is probable for Monday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Nesmith is likely to play Monday given his probable tag and he could even remain in the starting lineup. Still, he’s an unexciting player for fantasy purposes.

 Tyrese Haliburton, Andrew Nembhard, Aaron Nesmith, Pascal Siakam and Ivica Zubac will start Sunday’s game against the Nets. 
 After coming off the bench in his first appearance of the season on Friday, Nesmith reclaims his usual starting role in Brooklyn. Jarace Walker heads to the bench, and he may offer greater fantasy value as a reserve than as a starter.

 Aaron Nesmith (hamstring) is available for Sunday’s game against the Nets. 
 Nesmith made his first appearance of the season in Friday’s loss to the Mavericks, playing 20 minutes off the bench. The Pacers’ fifth starter has changed game to game, with Kelly Oubre Jr. starting the opener and Jarace Walker getting the nod on Friday. Depending on any potential injury management protocols, Nesmith could regain his spot in the starting five soon.

 Aaron Nesmith (hamstring) is probable to play against the Nets on Sunday. 
 Nesmith missed the season opener with this hamstring injury, but he was able to play on Friday despite a questionable tag. He played 20 minutes off the bench in that game and should play a similar role against Brooklyn. He should eventually replace Jarace Walker in the starting lineup, but it’s unclear if that will happen in this game. 
 Ben Sheppard 
 IND 
 Guard 
 #26 
 According to Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle, Ben Sheppard (knee) has no return timeline. 
 Despite the Pacers listing Sheppard as questionable for Friday’s game against the Mavericks, he’s expected to miss time with a left meniscus injury. Carlisle said on Friday that the reserve guard could miss two weeks or more. With Aaron Nesmith cleared to return from a strained hamstring, he’ll absorb most of the minutes that would have gone to Sheppard.

 Aaron Nesmith (hamstring) returned to practice on Thursday. 
 Nesmith, who missed the Pacers’ third preseason game with a hamstring injury, returned to practice on Thursday. He wasn’t available for Friday’s preseason finale against the Bucks, but his ability to practice bodes well for his availability for the regular-season opener on October 21. If Nesmith can’t play, Kelly Oubre Jr. would replace him in the starting lineup. 
 Aaron Nesmith 
 IND 
 Guard-Forward 
 #23 
 Aaron Nesmith accumulated a team-high 19 points (7-of-9 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs) across 15 minutes in Wednesday’s preseason win over the Timberwolves. 
 Nesmith shot nearly 78 percent from the floor, including 4-of-6 from three-point range, as the Pacers looked like a completely different operation with franchise icon Tyrese Haliburton finally back after missing all of last season with an Achilles injury. The 26-year-old wing was limited to just 45 games due to injury last year, but averaged a career-high 13.8 points per-game. That number should rise with Haliburton back running the offense and setting him up for additional open looks.

 DeMar DeRozan accounted for 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, two steals, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
 For the first time since his rookie season, DeRozan is being asked to come off the bench. As expected, the veteran forward needs to adjust to the unfamiliar role. After taking 19 shots in Denver’s first two games, he took 15 against the Warriors and recorded his first 20-point stat line of the season. As DeRozan gets more comfortable in his role, his chances of providing the fantasy value managers have grown accustomed to over the years improve. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Bryce Hopkins finished Monday’s loss to the Warriors with 13 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer.
 Monday’s start was the second in as many games for Hopkins, who continues to fill in for the injured Cameron Johnson (ankle). Unlike Saturday’s win over the Pelicans, when he offered limited production, the rookie was more aggressive on offense. The result was Hopkins’ first double-figure scoring night as an NBA player. He should remain a starter until Johnson is healthy enough to play. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jamal Murray notched 19 points (8-of-13 FGs), six rebounds, eight assists, three steals and three three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
 After going off for 42 points in Saturday’s win over the Pelicans, Murray cooled off a bit on Monday. However, he still shot well; the final line reflected lower shot volume and his inability to get to the foul line. After attempting 13 free throws against New Orleans, Murray didn’t attempt any against the Warriors. Monday’s outcome aside, Murray’s gotten off to a good individual start this season. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Nikola Jokić recorded 19 points (8-of-18 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, 11 assists, one steal, three blocks and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
 Two nights after recording a triple-double in Denver’s comeback win over the Pelicans, Jokić posted a double-double on Monday. The three-time MVP finished with a complete stat line and committed one turnover, a good start to the week for those rostering him. However, the Nuggets are now 1-2, and they needed to erase a large deficit to get that lone win. Simply put, Jokić needs more help from teammates not named Jamal Murray. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Brandin Podziemski recorded 18 points (7-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
 Back in the lineup after sitting out Saturday’s loss to the Suns, Podziemski recorded his second 18-point game of the season. He played 33 minutes against the Nuggets, a positive sign given the back issue that kept Podz out of the Warriors’ October 21 season opener. Golden State has three more games in Week 2, ending with a Sunday/Monday back-to-back, so another injury management night could be on the horizon for Podziemski. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Stephen Curry accounted for 24 points (8-of-8 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
 For just the second time in his illustrious career, Curry finished a game without missing a shot. After making his lone attempt during the first half, the Warriors guard shot 7-of-7 from the field in the second half as they pulled away from the Nuggets. Given Yaxel Lendeborg’s play, the Warriors didn’t have to rely as much on Curry. If that continues, it would make the future Hall of Fame guard’s job a little easier. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Yaxel Lendeborg finished Monday’s win over the Nuggets with 31 points (9-of-19 FGs, 12-of-13 Fts), 12 rebounds, six assists, one block and one three-pointer.
 On a night when Stephen Curry attempted just one shot in the first half, Lendeborg had his best game as a pro. The rookie forward recorded his second double-double in four games and his first 30-point stat line. Given Lendeborg’s role with the Warriors and how much the team seems to trust him, he could be one of the best rookies in fantasy basketball this season. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Mo Bamba started the second half and finished with 14 points (7-of-8 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist and four blocks on Monday against the Grizzlies.
 Both Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) and Lauri Markkanen (wrist) exited early from this game, which allowed Bamba and Josh Green to start the second half. Green wasn’t productive, but Bamba made the most of the opportunity. If Jackson remains out against the Spurs on Wednesday, Bamba may be in line to start. However, it is unlikely be produces to this level again, and the matchup against Victor Wembanyama isn’t ideal.

 Ace Bailey recorded a double-double on Monday with 17 points (6-of-10 FGs), 10 rebounds, three assists, three blocks and three three-pointers against the Grizzlies.
 Bailey has been excellent over Utah’s last two games, posting a double-double in both. However, his production could continue to climb. Lauri Markkanen (knee) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) both exited early from this game and could remain sidelined. Bailey already moved into the starting unit after opening night, but his usage will continue to increase if Utah is missing two starters. He’ll look to stay hot against the Spurs on Wednesday.
